headline: MD simulations localize residues and regions governing amyloid aggregation propensity
label: Molecular Dynamics Of Amyloid Aggregation
summary: Atomistic simulations now attribute amyloid aggregation propensity to specific residues and regions rather than to global net charge.
synthesis: The common thread is atomistic molecular dynamics used to localize residues and regions governing aggregation-prone interactions. A preprint applies all-atom MD to spermine on Tau K18, α-synuclein and Aβ40, reporting residue-specific rather than net-charge-driven control of fibril-like contacts. A published study simulates an Aβ hexamer with KLVFF, showing fibril-end binding that destabilizes terminal monomers, with CD and ThT assays supporting inhibition. A separate study combines 21 μs of MD and GaMD to map five aggregation-prone regions in the myocilin olfactomedin domain, linked to blade A destabilization. What is new is the attribution of propensity to specific residues and regions rather than to global charge. Evidence maturity differs: only the KLVFF study pairs simulation with experimental readouts.
